If you need someone who understands sight loss, RNIB (Royal National Institute of Blind People) is here for you. 

Everyone who is blind or partially sighted has their own unique experience, so we don’t take a one-size-fits-all approach. We offer a range of products and services to help you to maintain your independence and live the life you want to lead.

A service offered by selected pharmacies within the borough.

The service is available at the following pharmacies in Havering:  
·  Ardleigh Green Pharmacy, 100 Ardleigh Green Road, Hornchurch RM11 2LG

Varenicline:  Varenicline is a medication used to help you to stop smoking by reducing cravings and helping with withdrawal symptoms.  Taking Varenicline along with counselling provided by your pharmacist should increase your chance of quitting smoking for good.  The medication is taken daily with effects being noticed within a few days of beginning the course.  
For more information visit this NHS website:  https://www.nhs.uk/medicines/varenicline/about-varenicline/  
Varenicline is only available through the pharmacies listed and as part of the smoking cessation programme offer, it is not available through GP’s.

Free premium access to SmokeFree app:  For a limited period, smokers in Havering can get six months free access to SmokeFree app (premium version) ( https://app.smokefreeapp.com/code ), which has helped 500,000 people to give up smoking for good.  The app provides access to 24/7 real time support and 12 weeks of free nicotine replacement therapy or vapes, delivered to your door, at no extra cost.  

Stop Smoking London Helpline:  0300 123 1044   You can also visit the Stop Smoking London website ( https://stopsmokinglondon.com/ ) to learn more about the reasons you smoke and how you can use this to make a personalised quit plan.

Services.ServiceName: Alcohol addiction - support for family and friends

Metrics.ElementText:
DARS at HMP Liverpool is a free and confidential drug and alcohol service for adult offenders and their friends and family. Potential to change is always possible. At HMP Liverpool all offenders are made aware of the CGL DARS service, what we offer and how to access it.

DARS slots into the induction sessions that are held daily giving prisoners information on the service, various drug treatment programs on offer, referral into the community services and confidentiality arrangements. DARS welcomes referrals at any time during the offender’s sentence and we work with remands. Anyone can refer, and we welcome self referrals and family referrals.

We can look together at how to best stabilise or detox from methadone and on release we offer to make appointments for continuity of care and continuation of substitute prescribing. We work with offenders to help them reach their potential and enable them to take charge of their recovery journey.
Monday to Friday 8am - 4pm
North West Area Including Manchester

There is no open access drop-in available for this service. Offenders can put in an application to speak to a drug worker via their personal officer, or speak to any drug worker on the wing - they have purple CGL lanyards. External referrals can only be received by phone or email, not in person.

Metrics.ElementText:
DARS at HMP Liverpool is a free and confidential drug and alcohol service for adult offenders and their friends and family. Potential to change is always possible. At HMP Liverpool all offenders are made aware of the CGL DARS service, what we offer and how to access it.

DARS slots into the induction sessions that are held daily giving prisoners information on the service, various drug treatment programs on offer, referral into the community services and confidentiality arrangements. DARS welcomes referrals at any time during the offender’s sentence and we work with remands. Anyone can refer, and we welcome self referrals and family referrals.

We can look together at how to best stabilise or detox from methadone and on release we offer to make appointments for continuity of care and continuation of substitute prescribing. We work with offenders to help them reach their potential and enable them to take charge of their recovery journey.
Monday to Friday 8am - 4pm
North West Area Including Manchester

There is no open access drop-in available for this service. Offenders can put in an application to speak to a drug worker via their personal officer, or speak to any drug worker on the wing - they have purple CGL lanyards. External referrals can only be received by phone or email, not in person.

As a group we try to support each other through the sad times and share our good times. This is done with lots of coffee and biscuits and a very inclusive warm atmosphere.  We have weekly meetings and various monthly speakers, fund-raising events and social events; meals, trips, quiz nights,therapies.

The Migraine Trust is the largest research and support charity for people affected by migraine in the UK. Our role is to fund and promote new research into migraine, provide day-to-day support for people affected, and campaign for change. We provide evidence-based information and support – via our website and information– on all aspects of migraine and helping people with migraine experiencing difficulties at work, in education, or in accessing healthcare services.  

Our information services support people affected by migraine by providing information and support of a range of topics including diagnosis, treatment, accessing support, rights in education and employment and living well with migraine.

Metrics.ElementText:
The address listed on this page is the location of the local screening service office, not a screening clinic.

The service delivers diabetic eye screening in a variety of locations throughout the area, including GP surgeries, hospitals and optician practices.

All people aged 12 and over with diabetes (type 1 and 2) are offered annual eye screening appointments.

 The only exceptions are people with diabetic eye disease who are already under the care of an ophthalmology specialist.

 The screening test usually takes around 30 minutes. Screening does not replace regular eye examinations and it is important to attend both.

The NHS Business Services Authority is an Arm’s Length Body of the Department of Health and Social Care. We manage over £35 billion of NHS spend annually, delivering a range of national services to NHS organisations, NHS contractors, patients and the public. 
Our purpose is to be a catalyst for better health and our vision is to be the delivery partner of choice for the NHS.

Healthwatch is your health and social care champion. If you use GPs and hospitals, dentists, pharmacies, care homes or other support services, we want to hear about your experiences.

As an independent statutory body, we have the power to make sure NHS leaders and other decision makers listen to your feedback and improve standards of care.

We can also help you to reliable and trustworthy information and advice. Last year, we helped nearly a million people like you to have your say and get the support you need.

Wherever you live in England, you will have a local Healthwatch nearby (there are over 150 across the country). We are here to listen to the issues that really matter to local communities and to hear about your experiences of using health and social care services.

We are entirely independent and impartial, and any information you share with us is confidential. Healthwatch uses your feedback to better understand the challenges facing the NHS and other care providers nationally, to make sure your experiences improve health and care services for everyone.

We can also help you to get the information and advice you need to make the right decisions for you and to get the support you deserve.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.
This is a Practising Surgery

value.OrganisationName: Saint Mary's Sexual Assault Referral Centre - SARC

Services.ServiceName: Rape and sexual assault referral centre

Metrics.ElementText: Available 24 hours, call for advice or to make an appointment.

Sexual assault referral centres offer medical, practical and emotional support to anyone who has been sexually assaulted or raped. They have specially trained pediatrician / Forensic Nurse Examiners (FNE)  and support workers to care for you.
In an emergency you should always call 999. If you are unable to safely talk to the operator answering your 999 call, press 55 on your handset to let them know you are there.
Other

St Mary's Sexual Assault Referral Centre (SARC) provides a comprehensive and co-ordinated forensic, counselling and aftercare service to men, women and children living in the Greater Manchester and Cheshire area who have experienced rape or sexual assault, whether this has happened recently or in the past.

We understand that you may be feeling scared and frightened and that you may not feel able to trust anyone. At the Saint Mary’s Centre our main aim is to provide you with information, choice and control on what will happen to you. We want you to feel comfortable with the decisions you take. We will support you in your choices, whatever they may be.

Catch22 Hampshire 247 is a county-wide specialist treatment service offering targeted and specialist support to young people. We offer a tailored package of support to young people under 25 including one to one and group work support, a 24-hour help line, pharmacological support and needle exchange. Young people are at the centre of all we do. We ensure the young person knows they will be listened to at all times.

Our service is delivered by a multi professional team with a designated worker for each district of the county. The service offers a community engagement model, supporting children and young people where they feel most comfortable whilst working at their pace. Our is work is supported by our partnership with Inclusion Recovery Hampshire and Parent Support Link.

Under 18’s
Our service has a wide range of substance misuse interventions, offering young people confidential and non-judgemental support regarding the use of drugs and alcohol – to enable informed choice. We offer harm reduction advice and aim to improve the health and wellbeing of all the young people we work with.

We offer expertise to our wider partnerships such as youth offending teams, CAMHS, children’s services, youth support and education and can offer specific joined approaches for children at risk of criminal exploitation and wider health support such as smoking cessation, nutritional and sleep management.
18-25 years
Working in partnership with Inclusion Recovery Hampshire, we offer a designated transitional service for young adults aged 18 – 25 years. This work is supported by nurses, doctors, social work and clinical leads. Our expertise ensures every young person is offered an age appropriate service across all elements of service delivery.

Support provided
- 24/7 help line for young people: 0800 599 9591
- specialist harm reduction services
- individual tailored care plans and assessments
- family support
- access to prescribing and needle exchange
- auricular acupuncture
- one to one and group interventions in educational settings
- support within the community
- partnership working with agencies in Hampshire.
24 hour
Hampshire (excluding Portsmouth and Southampton Cities who are unitary authorities and commission their own services)
Anyone can refer to the service, including the young person themselves, but only if the young person has given their consent to the referral. Referrals can be made by telephone or email.

Build on Belief offers a range of socially based services for people who have, or have had alcohol and drug addiction issues; services run in the main by volunteers who have had problems themselves in the past.

How we can help
If you want to reduce, manage or stop using alcohol or other drugs, we are here for you. Our friendly and experienced team will work with you to find the right support for your needs.
We offer a range of free and confidential services, including:
·	Support with physical, emotional and mental health
·	Needle exchange
·	Recovery and detox programmes

·	Education, training and employment opportunities

Support for professionals

Metrics.ElementText:
Change Grow Live Manchester work with anyone looking to make positive changes related to drug & alcohol use. We approach treatment with an open mind, free from judgement. If your goals don't include treatment and recovery, but you do want to reduce the harmful impacts of drug & alcohol use, we can help with this too.  

Change Grow Live are a national organisation, with the aim to help people change the direction of their lives, grow as individuals and live life to its full potential. In Manchester, we offer support with harm reduction, needle exchange, housing, criminal justice, employment, education & training and homeless outreach. We have links with other services, including a smoking addiction service also under the Change Grow Live umbrella, called Be Smoke Free, and we offer a service which works specifically with young people, called Eclypse. We work with Emerging Futures and Acorn to deliver our psychosocial intervention groups and after-treatment care, and LGBT Foundation to provide specialist support related to LGBTQ+ issues for those in treatment. 

Change Grow Live's teams work in partnership with service users to assess their requirements and to plan individual treatment plans and support that will help service users to address their problems and achieve their personal goals.

We provide a full range of treatment and recovery interventions for people who require services for their drug or alcohol use. We do this by providing:

- Initial assessment to work out what support will benefit you
- Brief interventions (including harm reduction advice and support over the phone)
- Medically assisted treatment (MAT)
- Support sessions with recovery coordinators and engagement workers – one-to-one and in small groups
- Second opinions when requested by a GP
- Community detox
- Referral for in-patient detox
- Links to rehab clinics
- Peer Support groups – informal drop-ins, and structured group programmes
- Health assessments
- Blood-borne virus (BBV) tests and treatment - HIV, Hep B and Hep C
- Hep B vaccinations
- Needle Syringe Programmes (AKA needle exchange)

We also deliver free online training to professionals on topics related to drug & alcohol use, which you can find on our Eventbrite page:   https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/cc/adult-drug-alcohol-training-for-professionals-2132019
Monday to Friday, 9am – 5pm. Some evening openings available – please ring 0161 823 6306 for details
Manchester

We take referrals from any source as long as they’re with the person’s consent. Clients can also self refer to the service.

Please complete online referral form:  https://www.changegrowlive.org/manchester/referrals

Change Grow Live Manchester work with anyone looking to make positive changes related to drug & alcohol use. We approach treatment with an open mind, free from judgement. If your goals don't include treatment and recovery, but you do want to reduce the harmful impacts of drug & alcohol use, we can help with this too.  

Change Grow Live are a national organisation, with the aim to help people change the direction of their lives, grow as individuals and live life to its full potential. In Manchester, we offer support with harm reduction, needle exchange, housing, criminal justice, employment, education & training and homeless outreach. We have links with other services, including a smoking addiction service also under the Change Grow Live umbrella, called Be Smoke Free, and we offer a service which works specifically with young people, called Eclypse. We work with Emerging Futures and Acorn to deliver our psychosocial intervention groups and after-treatment care, and LGBT Foundation to provide specialist support related to LGBTQ+ issues for those in treatment. 

Change Grow Live's teams work in partnership with service users to assess their requirements and to plan individual treatment plans and support that will help service users to address their problems and achieve their personal goals.

We provide a full range of treatment and recovery interventions for people who require services for their drug or alcohol use. We do this by providing:

·	Initial assessment to work out what support will benefit you
·	Brief interventions (including harm reduction advice and support over the phone)
·	Medically assisted treatment (MAT)
·	Support sessions with recovery coordinators and engagement workers – one-to-one and in small groups
·	Second opinions when requested by a GP
·	Community detox
·	Referral for in-patient detox
·	Links to rehab clinics
·	Peer Support groups – informal drop-ins, and structured group programmes
·	Health assessments
·	Blood-borne virus (BBV) tests and treatment - HIV, Hep B and Hep C
·	Hep B vaccinations
·	Needle Syringe Programmes (AKA needle exchange)

We also deliver free online training to professionals on topics related to drug & alcohol use, which you can find on our Eventbrite page:  https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/cc/adult-drug-alcohol-training-for-professionals-2132019
Monday to Friday, 9am – 5pm.  Some evening openings available – please ring 0161 823 6306 for details.
Manchester

We take referrals from any source as long as they’re with the person’s consent. Clients can also self refer to the service.

Please complete online referral form:  https://www.changegrowlive.org/manchester/referrals

Services.ServiceName: Alcohol addiction - support for family and friends

Metrics.ElementText:
Change Grow Live offers an all-age service to everyone living in Nottinghamshire County who is experiencing challenges with drugs and/or alcohol. The service is holistic and includes support for individuals as well as children and families impacted by someone else’s substance misuse.

This is a free and confidential advice and support service.

Services available:
Harm reduction and needle exchange
Support from recovery experts
Health support from in house Doctors and Nurses
A specialist family service
Testing and treatment for blood borne viruses
Access to Naloxone kits
Connections to community partners to support your recovery.

Everyone coming to Change Grow Live can expect to receive:
A service tailored to their individual needs.
Access to advice, information, and a full recovery assessment; including assessment for detox and residential rehab provision.
Structured treatment including clinical and psychosocial interventions.
Emphasis on peer mentoring and visible recovery to support service users throughout their recovery journey.
Recovery planning.
Referral to other support services where relevant.
Referral to employment. training and education providers.

We have 3 hubs across Nottinghamshire for in-person visits:

County South Hub: Under one Roof, 3 Vine Terrace, Hucknall, Nottinghamshire NG15 7HN, Covering Gedling, Broxtowe, Rushcliffe and Hucknall.

West Nottinghamshire Hub: Unit 2 & 3 Sherwood Court, Sherwood Street, Mansfield, Nottinghamshire NG18 1ER, Covering Mansfield, Ashfield and Ollerton.

North Nottinghamshire Hub: Crown House, Ground Floor, Newcastle Avenue, Worksop S80 1ET, Covering Bassetlaw, Newark and Sherwood.

In addition to our main hubs we also offer appointments by arrangements in other accessible community locations, for more information please contact our single point of contact team on 0115 896 0798

Metrics.ElementText:
Catch22 Hampshire 247 is a county-wide specialist treatment service offering targeted and specialist support to young people. We offer a tailored package of support to young people under 25 including one to one and group work support, a 24-hour help line, pharmacological support and needle exchange. Young people are at the centre of all we do. We ensure the young person knows they will be listened to at all times.

Our service is delivered by a multi professional team with a designated worker for each district of the county. The service offers a community engagement model, supporting children and young people where they feel most comfortable whilst working at their pace. Our is work is supported by our partnership with Inclusion Recovery Hampshire and Parent Support Link.

Under 18’s
Our service has a wide range of substance misuse interventions, offering young people confidential and non-judgemental support regarding the use of drugs and alcohol – to enable informed choice. We offer harm reduction advice and aim to improve the health and wellbeing of all the young people we work with.
We offer expertise to our wider partnerships such as youth offending teams, CAMHS, children’s services, youth support and education and can offer specific joined approaches for children at risk of criminal exploitation and wider health support such as smoking cessation, nutritional and sleep management.

18-25 years
Working in partnership with Inclusion Recovery Hampshire, we offer a designated transitional service for young adults aged 18 – 25 years. This work is supported by nurses, doctors, social work and clinical leads. Our expertise ensures every young person is offered an age appropriate service across all elements of service delivery.

Support provided
- 24/7 help line for young people: 0800 599 9591
- specialist harm reduction services
- individual tailored care plans and assessments
- family support
- access to prescribing and needle exchange
- auricular acupuncture
- one to one and group interventions in educational settings
- support within the community
- partnership working with agencies in Hampshire.
24 hour
(excluding Portsmouth and Southampton Cities who are unitary authorities and commission their own services)
Anyone can refer to the service, including the young person themselves, but only if the young person has given their consent to the referral.  Referrals can be made by telephone or email

Metrics.ElementText:
Change Grow Live Birmingham is a free and confidential drug and alcohol service for adults. We offer treatment and recovery services to support anyone experiencing difficulties with substance misuse in a range of local community and clinical settings. Our recovery teams include doctors, non-medical prescribers, recovery coordinators, nurses, recovery motivators, service user representatives, and volunteers. We also work with Intuitive Thinking Skills, DATUS, and KIKIT to provide specialist support in our Throughcare offer.

We provide:
·	Confidential advice and information about drugs and alcohol
·	A tailored package of care
·	Healthcare clinics and blood-borne virus testing
·	Residential detoxification and rehabilitation options
·	Ambulatory detox in our hubs
·	Throughcare (group sessions from our recovery motivators and partners)
·	Harm minimisation
·	Needle Exchange and safe storage
·	Shared Care (121 sessions in your local GP surgery)

Depending on your situation, you may be referred to one of our in-house specialist teams. These teams include the Women’s and Families team, Criminal Justice, IPS Employment team, the Veteran’s group, Buvidal team and Homeless & Rough Sleeper team.

Metrics.ElementText:
ESCAPE Family Support provides trauma informed support and therapeutic services to all people whose lives have been affected by substance misuse including carers, parents, grandparents, friends, other family members and the children of substance users. We also provide parenting programmes and courses to address Adverse Childhood Experiences to substance using parents. Support required can be emotional, practical, psychological, social, healthcare, legal and financial. We provide specific support to kinship carers and to the bereaved. We have a dedicated Young Peoples Project to support young carers and children of substance users.

We are an AIM registered learning centre and deliver education and accredited training courses to peer mentors and volunteers.

Our Health and Wellbeing workshops help those in need to build confidence, improve self-esteem and believe in themselves. We  also run sessions in anger, anxiety and stress awareness as well as sleep hygiene to promote better coping strategies.

Metrics.ElementText:
We’re here to offer support without judgment, ensuring you have everything you need to kick-start your recovery journey. Using our unique shared experiences and high levels of training, we provide trusted support and advice to guide you and your family towards a life beyond drugs and alcohol.

We provide easily accessible and effective services covering most aspects of addiction – including drugs, alcohol and gambling. No matter who you are or how you got here, we’re here to support you and provide a welcoming and friendly place where you won’t be judged. We offer true flexibility and choice in appointments to make your recovery work for you, with fully equipped treatment rooms to help promote privacy and dignity in your appointments.
Single point of contact for those affected by drugs or alcohol. 

What can Spark Blackburn with Darwen do for you?

- We will complete a comprehensive assessment with you to try and find out what difficulties are in your life
- We will then devise a recovery care plan with you to take all of those needs into account
- We will work with you on a one-to-one basis to help you overcome your problems
- We will recommend different group work programmes for you
- We will refer you to, and link in with other services and organisations that can help you
- 
Fully integrated substance misuse treatment service available for all Blackburn with Darwen residents who have problems with their alcohol or drug use, or are worried about a family member, partner or friend. Our innovative service prides itself on getting to the root cause of your problems and helping you with your primary addiction, as well as offering help and support in other aspects of your life

Our services include:

Medical support during detox and rehab
-  We’ll be here throughout your recovery journey.
Clinical assessments and interventions
-  We check your health and can refer you to the right treatment service when required.
Psychological interventions
-  This helps us identify any problems and treat them quickly.
Detoxification
-  This involves removing drugs and alcohol from your system to help you get clean.
Rapid access prescriptions
-  We can help with urgent prescriptions, including methadone.
1-1 and Group services
-  Our professionals are here for confidential appointments throughout your recovery with us.

Young person specialist service: Early Break
We’re here Monday to Friday, 9am-5pm

Metrics.ElementText:
Build on Belief offers a range of socially based services for people who have, or have had alcohol and drug addiction issues; services run in the main by volunteers who have had problems themselves in the past. 

Services are designed to complement the existing treatment system, offering support, social interaction and a range of activities when there is often nowhere else for people to go, for example at the weekends. This can be a lonely and difficult time if you are in recovery and don’t know how to fill your time. The experience of addiction is often isolating and one of the main challenges in moving forward in your life is making new friends and building a good support network. BoB runs a number of social clubs in London where people with drug and alcohol problems (service users) can come and meet others in a similar situation.
See website for details of meeting times and locations.

Metrics.ElementText:
With You at Chy is a residential rehab for men and women who need support with addiction issues.

Our programme runs for 12 weeks. We offer one-to-one and group support, life skills workshops and training and education opportunities. Expert help is on hand 24 hours a day. 

There is a range of psycho-social interventions available, including therapeutic group work, workshops and counselling sessions delivered by BACP accredited counsellors. We also provide the RAFT programme, which is an eight-week intensive arts psychotherapy programme.

We are a dog friendly rehab with heated kennels, making our services better accessible to dog-owners. 

For those wishing to extend their therapeutic journey, residents can apply for one of our on-site move-on flats.

CQC rating of 'good overall'. 

Who’s this service for?
With You at Chy offers residential places for adults who have just done a detox.

We also provide follow-on support for people who are working towards independent living, with move-on flats on site and employment support.

We offer support for family members.

Lots of people who come to With You at Chy are funded by their local authority. We also welcome people who are funding themselves.
Monday to Friday 8am - 5pm
Cornwall and Isles of Scilly
You can self-refer by contacting WithYou in Cornwall directly, or you may be referred by your GP, another professional or a family member.

Barnsley Recovery Steps is a free and confidential service for people living in Barnsley, South Yorkshire. We are an all age service, supporting anyone who wants to change their relationship with alcohol or other drugs, and we are also here for people affected by someone else’s use.

How we can help
If you want to reduce, manage or stop using alcohol or other drugs, we are here for you. Our friendly and experienced team will work with you to find the right support for your needs.
We offer a range of free and confidential services, including:
·	Support with physical, emotional and mental health
·	Needle exchange
·	Recovery and detox programmes
·	One to one and group therapy
·	Help with housing and managing your money
·	Social activities
·	Education, training and employment opportunities

You can also contact us if you are worried about someone else's alcohol or drug use.

Support for young people
We have a dedicated young people’s team called SPACE, offering tailored support for anyone aged 10 to 18.

Making support more accessible
·	We have a hub in Goldthorpe for people who may struggle to access our central Barnsley locations
·	We also have a dedicated worker in North East Barnsley, focusing on making our support more accessible in that area

Support for professionals
Our HOPE team is here for professionals too, offering expert advice, guidance and training to help you better support the people you work with.

Who we support
This service is for you if:
·	You are aged 10 or over
·	You live in Barnsley
·	You are concerned about your own use or someone else’s

Services.ServiceName: Drug misuse - support for family and friends

Metrics.ElementText:
Change Grow Live Manchester work with anyone looking to make positive changes related to drug & alcohol use. We approach treatment with an open mind, free from judgement. If your goals don't include treatment and recovery, but you do want to reduce the harmful impacts of drug & alcohol use, we can help with this too.  

Change Grow Live are a national organisation, with the aim to help people change the direction of their lives, grow as individuals and live life to its full potential. In Manchester, we offer support with harm reduction, needle exchange, housing, criminal justice, employment, education & training and homeless outreach. We have links with other services, including a smoking addiction service also under the Change Grow Live umbrella, called Be Smoke Free, and we offer a service which works specifically with young people, called Eclypse. We work with Emerging Futures and Acorn to deliver our psychosocial intervention groups and after-treatment care, and LGBT Foundation to provide specialist support related to LGBTQ+ issues for those in treatment. 

Change Grow Live's teams work in partnership with service users to assess their requirements and to plan individual treatment plans and support that will help service users to address their problems and achieve their personal goals.

We provide a full range of treatment and recovery interventions for people who require services for their drug or alcohol use. We do this by providing:

- Initial assessment to work out what support will benefit you
- Brief interventions (including harm reduction advice and support over the phone)
- Medically assisted treatment (MAT)
- Support sessions with recovery coordinators and engagement workers – one-to-one and in small groups
- Second opinions when requested by a GP
- Community detox
- Referral for in-patient detox
- Links to rehab clinics
- Peer Support groups – informal drop-ins, and structured group programmes
- Health assessments
- Blood-borne virus (BBV) tests and treatment - HIV, Hep B and Hep C
- Hep B vaccinations
- Needle Syringe Programmes (AKA needle exchange)

We also deliver free online training to professionals on topics related to drug & alcohol use, which you can find on our Eventbrite page:   https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/cc/adult-drug-alcohol-training-for-professionals-2132019
Monday to Friday, 9am – 5pm. Some evening openings available – please ring 0161 823 6306 for details
Manchester

We take referrals from any source as long as they’re with the person’s consent. Clients can also self refer to the service.

Please complete online referral form:  https://www.changegrowlive.org/manchester/referrals

A specialist family service

Metrics.ElementText:
We’re here to offer support without judgment, ensuring you have everything you need to kick-start your recovery journey. Using our unique shared experiences and high levels of training, we provide trusted support and advice to guide you and your family towards a life beyond drugs and alcohol.

We provide easily accessible and effective services covering most aspects of addiction – including drugs, alcohol and gambling. No matter who you are or how you got here, we’re here to support you and provide a welcoming and friendly place where you won’t be judged. We offer true flexibility and choice in appointments to make your recovery work for you, with fully equipped treatment rooms to help promote privacy and dignity in your appointments.
Single point of contact for those affected by drugs or alcohol. 

What can Spark Blackburn with Darwen do for you?

- We will complete a comprehensive assessment with you to try and find out what difficulties are in your life
- We will then devise a recovery care plan with you to take all of those needs into account
- We will work with you on a one-to-one basis to help you overcome your problems
- We will recommend different group work programmes for you
- We will refer you to, and link in with other services and organisations that can help you
- 
Fully integrated substance misuse treatment service available for all Blackburn with Darwen residents who have problems with their alcohol or drug use, or are worried about a family member, partner or friend. Our innovative service prides itself on getting to the root cause of your problems and helping you with your primary addiction, as well as offering help and support in other aspects of your life

Our services include:

Medical support during detox and rehab
-  We’ll be here throughout your recovery journey.
Clinical assessments and interventions
-  We check your health and can refer you to the right treatment service when required.

Metrics.ElementText:
Change Grow Live Manchester work with anyone looking to make positive changes related to drug & alcohol use. We approach treatment with an open mind, free from judgement. If your goals don't include treatment and recovery, but you do want to reduce the harmful impacts of drug & alcohol use, we can help with this too.  

Change Grow Live are a national organisation, with the aim to help people change the direction of their lives, grow as individuals and live life to its full potential. In Manchester, we offer support with harm reduction, needle exchange, housing, criminal justice, employment, education & training and homeless outreach. We have links with other services, including a smoking addiction service also under the Change Grow Live umbrella, called Be Smoke Free, and we offer a service which works specifically with young people, called Eclypse. We work with Emerging Futures and Acorn to deliver our psychosocial intervention groups and after-treatment care, and LGBT Foundation to provide specialist support related to LGBTQ+ issues for those in treatment. 

Change Grow Live's teams work in partnership with service users to assess their requirements and to plan individual treatment plans and support that will help service users to address their problems and achieve their personal goals.

We provide a full range of treatment and recovery interventions for people who require services for their drug or alcohol use. We do this by providing:

·	Initial assessment to work out what support will benefit you
·	Brief interventions (including harm reduction advice and support over the phone)
·	Medically assisted treatment (MAT)
·	Support sessions with recovery coordinators and engagement workers – one-to-one and in small groups
·	Second opinions when requested by a GP
·	Community detox
·	Referral for in-patient detox
·	Links to rehab clinics
·	Peer Support groups – informal drop-ins, and structured group programmes
·	Health assessments
·	Blood-borne virus (BBV) tests and treatment - HIV, Hep B and Hep C
·	Hep B vaccinations
·	Needle Syringe Programmes (AKA needle exchange)

We also deliver free online training to professionals on topics related to drug & alcohol use, which you can find on our Eventbrite page:  https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/cc/adult-drug-alcohol-training-for-professionals-2132019
Monday to Friday, 9am – 5pm.  Some evening openings available – please ring 0161 823 6306 for details.
Manchester

value.OrganisationName: Mrs A O Tinker MRCPod BSc(Hons)

Metrics.ElementText:
The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.
This is a Practising Surgery

Services.ServiceName: Rape and sexual assault referral centre

Metrics.ElementText: Available 24 hours, call for advice or to make an appointment.

Sexual assault referral centres offer medical, practical and emotional support to anyone who has been sexually assaulted or raped. They have specially trained pediatrician / Forensic Nurse Examiners (FNE)  and support workers to care for you.
In an emergency you should always call 999. If you are unable to safely talk to the operator answering your 999 call, press 55 on your handset to let them know you are there.
Other

Northumbria Sexual Assault Referral Centre (SARC) offers help to men and women who have been raped or sexually assaulted, aged 16 or over when the assault occurred. The centres are staffed by people who are supportive and they will be happy to help you whether or not you wish to report to the police. The service is free and confidential.

The Patient Advice and Liaison Service, known as PALS, has been introduced to ensure that the NHS listens to patients, their relatives, carers and friends, and answers their questions and resolves their concerns as quickly as possible.
PALS also helps the NHS to improve services by listening to what matters to patients and their loved ones and making changes, when appropriate.

If you or someone on your behalf has questions or is unhappy with the care you receive we actively promote that in the first instance you talk directly to the staff involved in your treatment and care. Very often problems can be resolved straight away. If you do not feel able to raise your concerns directly with the staff within the ward or department where you are receiving treatment or you do not know who to speak to you can contact the PALS Service. The PALS Service is a non-clinical point of contact within the hospital for anyone requiring advice or assistance in relation to services provided by our Trust. It is there to provide information in response to queries and ensure concerns and problems are resolved as quickly as possible by the relevant department or service within the hospital.
      If possible PALS will provide on the spot advice or information or signpost you to help resolve the issues. If your concerns cannot be addressed directly by the PALS staff they will coordinate sending your concerns to the most appropriate department/manager. It is the responsibility of the department/manager to respond directly to you and ensure your questions or concerns are fully addressed.
Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust

Services.ServiceName: Drug misuse - support for family and friends

Metrics.ElementText:
Bromley Changes offers a range of treatment and support services for young people aged up to 18 who have concerns about their drug or alcohol use and are residents or have links in the borough of Bromley.

Service offers:
• Confidential advice and information for young people up to the age of 18
• Support to help you make informed decisions about your drug and alcohol use
• Support to help you cut down or stop using drugs or alcohol
• Assessment of your specific needs
• One-to-one sessions and group work
• Appointments at a convenient location
• Gateway to other services
• Drop-in services across the borough (please contact us for more details)
• Advice and information for parents and carers
• Male and female workers

There are also some new roles on the team which have improved the ways we can reach young people and their families.

• A youth criminal justice substance use worker- who has specialist knowledge to support young people in trouble with the law – from early prevention to working with young people offending in the CJS. 
•  Part of her role is to discuss and explore with young person the linked risk taking of using drugs and alcohol and committing offences and reducing overall risk of their behaviours, also delivers training to professionals on all things substance use and criminal justice related. 

A family  and carers worker attached to team- provides advisory and support service for parents whose children are misusing substances – running virtual parent support groups and offer of 1-1 work, with aim of promoting confident, drugs aware  parents 

• Hidden Harm worker-  offer of support for children age 5-18, support  for those affected by someone elses substance use a parent or carer, sibling. The young person doesn’t have to live with the adult they have been affected by but this is a really important early intervention service offered: tramua informed practise working at building emotional resilience young people and children  to process and heal from challenging life circumstances or cope with reality of living with an adult substance user.
Monday to Friday 9am - 5pm

CGL (Change Grow Live) Bromley provides an integrated treatment system for adults who have a problem with drug and alcohol use. The service works with people at all points of their treatment journey from engagement into services to recovery. We also provide support services to family and carers whose lives are affected by another’s drug and alcohol use. We offer a variety of treatment services including:

• Assessment 
• Open access 
• Outreach services 
• Opiate substitute prescribing 
• Community alcohol detoxification 
• Keyworking 
• Counselling 
• Group work 
• Job clubs 
• Peer support 
• Computer access and training 
• Ear acupuncture

Bromley Changes offers a range of treatment and support services for young people aged up to 18 who have concerns about their drug or alcohol use and are residents or have links in the borough of Bromley.

Service offers:
• Confidential advice and information for young people up to the age of 18

• Support to help you cut down or stop using drugs or alcohol
• Assessment of your specific needs
• One-to-one sessions and group work
• Appointments at a convenient location
• Gateway to other services

• Advice and information for parents and carers
• Male and female workers

There are also some new roles on the team which have improved the ways we can reach young people and their families.

• A youth criminal justice substance use worker- who has specialist knowledge to support young people in trouble with the law – from early prevention to working with young people offending in the CJS. 
•  Part of her role is to discuss and explore with young person the linked risk taking of using drugs and alcohol and committing offences and reducing overall risk of their behaviours, also delivers training to professionals on all things substance use and criminal justice related. 

A family  and carers worker attached to team- provides advisory and support service for parents whose children are misusing substances – running virtual parent support groups and offer of 1-1 work, with aim of promoting confident, drugs aware  parents 

• Hidden Harm worker-  offer of support for children age 5-18, support  for those affected by someone elses substance use a parent or carer, sibling. The young person doesn’t have to live with the adult they have been affected by but this is a really important early intervention service offered: tramua informed practise working at building emotional resilience young people and children  to process and heal from challenging life circumstances or cope with reality of living with an adult substance user.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.
This is a Practising Surgery

Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.
This is a Practising Surgery

Services.ServiceName: Alcohol addiction - support for family and friends

Metrics.ElementText:
Worried about your own or someone else’s alcohol or drug use? We offer free and confidential advice, support and treatment for people in Gloucestershire aged 18+.

We’ll talk about your concerns and make a plan together. This care plan will help you reduce or stop your drug or alcohol use – making sure you receive the right support at the right time for you. Help and advice for family, friends and carers on how best to support you during your recovery is also available.

At our service, you can get:

- Advice about your health and wellbeing
- Regular sessions with your personal keyworker
- A range of different support groups
- Women-only support and safe spaces in partnership with The Nelson Trust.
Gloucestershire
You can visit our service in person or contact us by phone or email. Any professional, such as a housing support worker, social worker, GP or nurse can also make a referral for you.

Services.ServiceName: Mental health services for alcohol addiction

Metrics.ElementText:
The Kingston Wellbeing Service offers free and confidential support to people in Kingston aged 18+ affected by drug and alcohol use. 

Services available include: 
• One-to-one support & treatment 
• Alcohol screening and assessment 
• Access to prescribing appointments 
• Assessment and preparation for detox and residential rehab 
• Advice about your health and wellbeing
• Regular sessions with your personal keyworker
• A range of different support groups
• Integrated Offender Management (IOM) programme 
• Assessment and referral for mental health issues

Monday to Friday 9am - 5pm
24/7 Referral Line on 0800 840 6704
The service is open to individuals aged 18+ and who live in the London Borough of Kingston.
The Gateway Service acts as the single point of referral for anyone experiencing problems with drugs and alcohol, including people who come through the criminal justice system.

We are the only patient-led, UK-wide charity representing people with Prostate Cancer and those who care for them

The Prostate Cancer Support Federation is the parent organisation of UK patient-led prostate cancer support groups. It provides resources to local patient-led support groups and is the only UK-wide patient-led charity that acts and speaks for prostate cancer patients and their families. Helpline support by telephone and e-mail is offered to men with prostate cancer, wives, partners and families, people who are concerned, and those who want to know more. Helpline support is given by volunteers who have themselves been affected by prostate cancer. Through the helpline you can be put in touch with contacts who have personal experience of the main treatments and stages of prostate cancer.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.
